decision: Implementation of test-leak-audit meets the release bar

state.change_summary:
Branch audit-testleak. Two deliverables.

1. A read-only audit of cross-test fragility across frontend/src and backend/tests,
   written to orchestration/decisions/test-leak-audit.md. It establishes by
   measurement that the cross-test mechanism in this suite is the shared jsdom
   global, not the module registry: a bare global.fetch assignment in one test
   file is visible to the next file in the same worker, while module-scope mutable
   state is not, because vitest's isolate defaults to true and rebuilds the module
   registry per file. TASK.md's stated premise for the module-state half is
   therefore incorrect, and the audit says so. 19 of 27 files that install fetch
   do so by plain assignment, which no restore mechanism can undo; 2 of these are
   shared helper modules with 8 consumers between them. In the backend, 3
   site-pairs of fixed dates are compared against a real clock across an HTTP
   boundary that never pins one, while ~70 further modules pin a clock and are
   inert. The repo has already solved this pattern seven times, and the
   distinguishing mechanism is dependency_overrides on the engine getter; the
   fragile modules are exactly the ones that omit it.

2. One fix, in backend/tests/test_wf056.py, which WF-056 owns. Not a shared file.
   14 tests posted a session window of the literal 2026-10-05T08:00:00Z and
   asserted a non-empty slot offer, while the route builds its engine with no
   clock (features/wf056_*.py:130 -> engine.py:114 self._clock = clock or
   _utcnow). Traced to availability.py:246-251, which returns an empty list once
   now + lead_minutes reaches the end of the window. Measured by sweeping now
   through the product's own slots() function: at a real now of
   2026-10-05T12:55:39Z the offer held 7 slots, and goes empty at
   2026-10-05T16:00:39Z, about 3h05m later. This is incident (a) from TASK.md,
   recorded there as repaired by PR #240; the feature was repaired and the 14
   test fixtures were not. The fixture now pins the engine clock through
   dependency_overrides on get_headless, the 14 literals became one constant
   derived from the file's existing NOW, and one new test asserts the override is
   in force. No test was weakened, skipped or deleted; every assertion is
   unchanged. No fixed date was introduced.

Contract note: the change edits one existing file, backend/tests/test_wf056.py,
which is a workflow-owned test file, not a shared file. None of backend/dsr/api.py,
deps.py, store.py, db/audited.py, backend/seed.py, App.jsx, main.jsx, lib/api.js,
lib/features.js, components/ui.jsx, vite.config.js or the shared test setup was
touched. The highest-leverage frontend fix is deliberately NOT applied: it is one
line in the shared frontend/src/test/setup.js, which TASK.md forbids editing, so
it is reported for a separate decision.

Adjudication of the three reported incidents: WF-056 is confirmed live and is
fixed here. WF-086 and WF-066 are recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than assigned.
The WF-066 report could not be reproduced: PR 237's branch is fully green at its
tip, its 9 red tests at the previous commit were all WF-083's own, and a probe
planting a never-resolving fetch immediately before the file in one process left
it 24/24 passing, because its renderPage() reassigns global.fetch before every
render. A real armed landmine of the right shape exists at ConsentGate.test.jsx:389
on that open PR, but no causal link to the reported failure was demonstrated, and
none is claimed.

declared_unverified: The two reported frontend incidents (WF-086 on PR 238, WF-066 on PR 237) are UNRESOLVED. Neither was reproduced. No cause is claimed for either, and the audit declines to assign one.

ConsentGate.test.jsx:389 on PR 237 is described as an armed landmine of the correct shape. That it is armed is traced and measured. That it CAUSED the WF-066 failure is NOT demonstrated, and is not asserted.

The backend sweep across all 118 test modules was performed by a delegated read-only agent. The headline finding (test_wf056.py, 14 sites) was independently re-verified end to end by direct reading and by measurement. The remaining backend line numbers, including BE-2 through BE-12, were returned by that sweep and were not each independently re-read by the orchestrator. They should be spot-checked before anyone acts on BE-5 through BE-10 specifically.

The ~70 inert pinned-clock modules were each confirmed to pass NOW explicitly into the code under test, which makes them deterministic, but the injection site was not opened for every one of them individually.

No frontend fix was applied. FE-1 through FE-9 are argued from the measured mechanism plus code reading; none was made to detonate on demand, because choosing a victim file is the error that caused the original incidents.

The probe that first appeared to show no global leak was running in the wrong order. That negative result was discarded and the probe re-run in a forced order before any conclusion was drawn. Recorded because it is the most likely way this audit could itself have produced a false clean result.

The full backend suite re-run after the change had not completed when this gate was called. test_wf056.py was verified green in full (345 passed) and ruff is clean; the whole-suite re-run is the outstanding item.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

reason: chose 'merge' but confidence 0.50 < 0.75; insufficient evidence to gate on

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
